newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends down on stop-loss selling.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends down on stop-loss selling.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended down on stop-loss selling on Monday after last Friday's sharp fall, traders said.
The most active January 1997 contract ended at 20,420 yuan ($2,458) per tonne, down 80 yuan. It opened at an intra-day low of 20,400 and hit a high of 20,560.
September closed unchanged at 21,200 yuan, October fell 30 to 20,770, November 20 to 20,500, December 40 to 20,440, February 80 to 20,420 and March 40 to 20,480.
Combined volume fell sharply to 21,090 tonnes from 121,750 tonnes.
Traders said that most long-positions holders had to liquidate their positions after sharp losses last Friday, which caused today's falls.
They said that copper would have a technical rebound in the short term on over-selling after continuous losses.
"Copper will meet strong support around the 20,000-yuan level because some end-users are willing to buy spot copper at that price," one trader said.
Aluminium ended down. September fell 120 to 14,180 yuan, October 30 to 14,270 and November closed unchanged at 14,320.
Combined volume unchanged at 610 tonnes.($1=8.3055 yuan)
